source.title: Do Deep Learning Models Have Too Many Parameters? An Information Theory Viewpoint

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses random-label fitting and reports its own variational-codelength experiment on random labels, but does not measure the claim versions’ training-error or generalization outcomes.
record.gate_note: The introduction states that convolutional networks can reach 100% training accuracy on random labels, citing Zhang et al. (2017); that cited result is not this paper’s own result. Figure 1 reports this paper’s variational-codelength experiment on true and fake labels, which does not establish whether the networks fit random labels to zero training error.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 measures variational codelength, including parameter cost, rather than random-label training accuracy. Its convergence to uniform encoding cannot establish whether V1–V6 hold. The caption also states that this MLP can overfit random labels under ordinary SGD, but gives no fitting accuracy or controlled comparison; the introduction attributes 100% training accuracy to Zhang et al.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that deep networks can compress real labels while accounting for the model, and that prequential coding gives substantially better compression than variational inference. Figure 1 and Appendix A address random-label incompressibility. The record's attribution needs qualification: the introduction cites Zhang et al. for 100% random-label training accuracy, while Figure 1 separately asserts that its MLP can overfit random labels with ordinary SGD, without reporting an accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper’s random-label experiment uses variational learning to measure codelength; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting intervention or measure its training and test errors.
record.method_sensitivity: The Figure 1 result contrasts true and fake labels and reports ordinary SGD overfitting only as background; no tested sensitivity sweep for the claim versions is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: For the MNIST MLP trained variationally, fake-label codelength converges to uniform encoding and the parameter-encoding contribution vanishes; true labels achieve compression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variational learning yields no compression of random labels in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A gives a counting argument that uniformly sampled independent labels are incompressible with high probability, even given the inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random labels generally admit no substantially shorter lossless description, regardless of whether a network can memorize them.

record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: The random-label plot provides no numeric values in the supplied text and measures variational codelength rather than training or test error. The ordinary-SGD fitting statement is attributed to prior work, not reported as this study’s own result.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero random-label training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing those regularizers.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels. Figure 1 compares codelength trajectories, not the order in which signal and noise are fitted.

record.verdict_notes: Incompressibility and memorization are compatible: encoding costs include the model or its equivalent information. The codelength result therefore supplies no challenge to random-label fitting.

versions.untested_parts: Training error, test error, and whether fitting required changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time versus true labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction changes.
Training on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across corruption fractions, including whether training error stays perfect.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: MLP with 3 hidden layers of size 200, with RELU units
rows.operation_detail: Variational learning on MNIST with true and fake labels; plotted the variational objective and parameter-encoding contribution.
rows.measure: Variational codelength per sample; the figure description says it converges to a uniform random model.
rows.note: The measured codelength does not establish training error or test error. The figure description explicitly states the qualitative result; no numeric value is given in the text.
rows.check: The subject, condition and qualitative codelength result are correctly recorded. Total variational codelength is not training error, so convergence to uniform encoding does not establish absence of random-label fitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
